To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chronic exposure of rats to ethanol in a noisy environment modifies the anxiolytic response, but not hypoactivity, observed on withdrawal from ethanol treatment.
chronic noise exposure during chronic ethanol treatment modifies the anxiogenesis detected on withdrawal from ethanol, but it has no effect on the hypoactivity.
chronic exposure to ethanol and chronic exposure to noise interact to produce anxiogenic effects on ethanol withdrawal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chronic ethanol treatment on the adaptive responses of rats to a variety of stimuli.
the effect of chronic exposure to noise on ethanol dependence, as assessed by the social interaction and plus-maze tests.
the effects of chronic noise exposure on ethanol withdrawal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chronic noise exposure during chronic alcohol treatment modifies the anxiogenecity of ethanol withdrawal, but not the motor activity, and this modification is not simply a delayed anxiogenic response.
chronic ethanol exposure in noisy environments does not alter the hypoactive response, but modifies the anxiolytic response, of ethanol withdrawal.
the anxiolytic effect of ethanol is suppressed by chronic noise exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

chronic ethanol treatment induces a hypoactivity and anxiogenic response in the social interaction test, and that chronic exposure to high levels of noise suppresses the hypoactivity, but not the anxiogenic, response.
noise suppresses the adaptive changes induced by ethanol treatment, but only in the pathways mediating anxiety.
chronic exposure to ethanol modifies the adaptive response, but only in the pathways mediating anxiety, and this is dependent on the housing conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environment can have a profound influence on the way that an organism responds to an addictive drug.
chronic noise exposure modifies the anxiolytic response to chronic ethanol treatment, and this effect can be observed in the absence of a change in the hypoactivity response.
the environment in which animals are treated can modify their response to the effects of drugs.
